title: Testing on small screens, emulators and real phones
when: Before release the phone app must be checked on narrow screens, both phone OSes, slow networks and real hardware, with results written down.
prompt:
Goal: TESTING-MOBILE.md, a repeatable device matrix and checklist, plus a tiny script that flags horizontal overflow.
Steps:
1. Viewport matrix: 320x568 (smallest), 360x800, 390x844, 412x915 and one tablet, each in portrait and landscape.
2. Start in the browser devtools device mode for layout, then confirm on real phones; touch, keyboards and performance differ on hardware.
3. Emulators and simulators come with the platform SDKs and their IDEs; the simulator for one phone OS needs a mac, so plan a real device or a cloud device lab.
4. Debug a real phone over USB with remote debugging and use a LAN URL for the dev server.
5. Run each flow with slow 4G throttling, airplane mode, system text at largest, dark mode and the screen reader on.
6. overflow-check.js: when document.documentElement.scrollWidth > window.innerWidth, list elements whose getBoundingClientRect().right exceeds innerWidth.
7. Check the keyboard: focused inputs stay visible and the submit button is reachable.
8. Record result per cell as pass, fail with a screenshot path, or not run.
Quality bar:
- The smallest viewport has no horizontal scroll.
- At least one real device per phone OS before release.
Pitfalls:
- Testing only the developer phone.
- Trusting the emulator for battery and speed.
Verify:
- [ ] The matrix lists sizes and orientations.
- [ ] overflow-check.js parses and reports elements.
- [ ] Every flow has a result per device.
Output: TESTING-MOBILE.md and overflow-check.js.

examples.input: como testo meu app em celular pequeno sem ter todos os aparelhos?
examples.output: TESTING-MOBILE.md matrix 320 to 412 px both orientations, emulator notes, overflow-check.js
